title: 1958 AHSME Problem 44
statement:
Given the true statements:

\(1.\) If \(a\) is greater than \(b,\) then \(c\) is greater than \(d.\)

\(2.\) If \(c\) is less than \(d,\) then \(e\) is greater than \(f.\)

A valid conclusion is:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
If \(a\) is less than \(b,\) then \(e\) is greater than
\(f\)

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
If \(e\) is greater than \(f,\) then \(a\) is less than
\(b\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
If \(e\) is less than \(f,\) then \(a\) is greater than
\(b\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
If \(a\) is greater than \(b,\) then \(e\) is less than
\(f\)

solutions.text:
Let \(P\) mean \(a>b,\) \(Q\) mean \(c>d,\) \(S\) mean \(c<d,\) and \(R\) mean \(e>f.\) The premises are \[ P\Rightarrow Q,\qquad S\Rightarrow R. \] The statements \(Q\) and \(S\) cannot both hold. The contrapositives are \(
eg Q\Rightarrow
eg P\) and \(
eg R\Rightarrow
eg S.\) None of the four proposed implications follows. For example, knowing \(P\) gives \(Q\) and hence \(
eg S,\) but says nothing about \(R;\) knowing \(
eg R\) gives \(
eg S,\) not \(P.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Represent the comparisons as propositions and distinguish each implication from its converse
The second premise’s hypothesis is incompatible with the first premise’s conclusion, but that alone does not chain the implications
